info.name: litellm
info.description:
LiteLLM proxy endpoints for this deployment. Config is in `ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml`; operator guide in `ai/litellm/LITELLM.md`; MCP tool-call orchestration in `ai/litellm/LITELLM_MCP.md`.

Auth model: the collection's default Bearer is `virtual master key` — an sk-… issued from the LiteLLM Admin UI → Virtual Keys (or `/key/generate`). Admin endpoints (under the `Admin` folder) override at the item level to `litellm master key` — the value of `DEFAULT_LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` in `.env`, which `general_settings.master_key` reads via `os.environ`. Never distribute the master key; use it only for key/user/model management.

Set the collection variables `litellm` (base URL — localhost publish is 4001 = `PORT_LITELLM`; the same API over TLS is https://api.zeoenergy.com, one URL in and out of the office (split-horizon DNS: on the office LAN the router's DNS override sends it to the edge on host port 443 = `PORT_LITELLM_TLS` with a Let's Encrypt certificate; anywhere else public DNS sends it through the Cloudflare tunnel to litellm:4000, whose responses carry `cf-ray` and are cut at Cloudflare's ~100 s origin timeout), see ai/edge/EDGE.md § TLS; on `ai_shared` it's http://litellm:4000), `virtual master key`, and `litellm master key` before running requests.

Models enabled in this deployment (from `model_list`): `kokoro` (TTS, audio); on vLLM `qwen3.6`, `qwen3.8`, `qwen3.8-solo`, `muse-glimmer` (vision) and `qwen2.5-vl` (image); on llama.cpp `glm5.2`, `qwen3.8-flash` and `glm5.3-flash`; `claude-sonnet-5` (Anthropic fallback) and `claude-opus-5-5`; the chain aliases below; plus the env-driven default (`DEFAULT_LITELLM_MODEL_NAME`). Context-window fallbacks route qwen3.6 / qwen3.8 / qwen3.8-solo / qwen3.8-flash / glm5.2 / glm5.3-flash / muse-glimmer → claude-sonnet-5 when the request exceeds the local model's window (see `litellm_settings.context_window_fallbacks`).

CHAIN ALIASES (folder 'Chain aliases'): local-general, local-code, local-reasoning, local-private are model groups whose deployments carry `order: 1 / 2 / 3` -- local vLLM first, Claude only when both local models are busy or down (overflow hook ai/litellm/overflow.py), and local-private never reaches Claude. The route-policy engine routes `auto` to one of them (the LiteLLM hook awaits its /decide and rewrites the model, in the same pass); you can also call them directly by name. See LITELLM.md > Chain aliases and the overflow hook.

**Error bodies.** Each endpoint's `#### Schemas` section -- at the end of its first request's description, generated from `litellm.schemas.json` by `scripts/api_schemas.py render` -- documents the fields this stack uses of each request and response body: an open subset of LiteLLM's API. LiteLLM's own errors answer `{"error": {"message", "type", "param", "code"}}` and are not repeated per endpoint; a pass-through route's error comes from the service behind it (that service's collection).

variable.description: LiteLLM base URL. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); over TLS https://api.zeoenergy.com (= https://<EDGE_TLS_DOMAIN>, host port 443 = PORT_LITELLM_TLS on the LAN edge; off the LAN the same URL goes through the cloudflared tunnel -- same requests, same keys; ai/edge/EDGE.md § TLS); on ai_shared it's http://litellm:4000. See ai/litellm/LITELLM.md § Quick start.

LiteLLM virtual key (Admin UI → Virtual Keys, or POST /key/generate). Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}` by the collection-level auth. Use this for all runtime / model / pass-through / MCP calls.

The proxy's admin master key — value of `DEFAULT_LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` in `.env`, read by `general_settings.master_key` in litellm_config.yaml. Required for /key/*, /user/*, /model/* admin endpoints. Do NOT distribute; scope tokens for downstream services via /key/generate instead.
Virtual-key token returned by POST /key/generate as `key`. Paste in to run /key/info, /key/update, /key/delete without editing each URL.
user_id assigned to a virtual key at creation, or a pre-existing user in the LiteLLM DB. Consumed by GET /user/info.

item.name: Health
item.description: Liveness / readiness probes. `/health/liveliness` is the container's docker healthcheck target (see LITELLM.md § Health checks). `/health` runs an actual upstream ping against configured models — slower, use for diagnostics not for uptime dashboards.

item.name: OpenAI-compatible
item.description: The primary API surface. LiteLLM presents an OpenAI-compatible interface in front of vLLM (qwen3.6, qwen3.8, qwen3.8-solo, muse-glimmer, qwen2.5-vl), llama.cpp (glm5.2, qwen3.8-flash, glm5.3-flash), Kokoro TTS, and Anthropic (claude-sonnet-5 fallback, claude-opus-5-5 opt-in). Models available are those enumerated under `model_list` in litellm_config.yaml. See LITELLM.md § `litellm_config.yaml` settings for the config schema reference.

request.description:
Kick off an MCP-backed tool call. When an `mcp_servers` entry is configured (e.g. `phoenix`), the model receives the tool definitions automatically and returns `finish_reason: tool_calls` with a `tool_call_id`. LiteLLM does NOT execute the call — copy the id and follow up with the step-2 request below. See LITELLM_MCP.md § Step 1: Send the user message.

#### Schemas

See *OpenAI-compatible / POST /v1/chat/completions*, the first request of this endpoint.

Send the tool result back. Replace `CALL_ID_FROM_STEP_1` with the id from the step-1 response, and put the actual MCP-tool result string in the `tool` message's `content`. LiteLLM feeds this back to the model, which returns a natural-language response. See LITELLM_MCP.md § Step 2: Send the tool result back.

#### Schemas

See *OpenAI-compatible / POST /v1/chat/completions*, the first request of this endpoint.

OpenAI-compatible text-to-speech. Routes to the `kokoro` model entry, which points at `http://kokoro-api:8000/v1` with `mode: audio`. Response is binary audio (use Postman's Send-and-Download). Kokoro also exposes an MCP server registered under `mcp_servers.kokoro_tts` — see the MCP folder for that path.

#### Schemas

Routed by `model` (`kokoro` -> kokoro-api's `POST /v1/audio/speech`, kokoro.schemas.json).

Request body (`application/json`):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": true,
  "required": ["model", "input"],
  "properties": {
    "model": {"type": "string", "description": "`kokoro`"},
    "input": {"type": "string", "description": "The text to speak"},
    "voice": {"type": "string", "description": "An OpenAI alias or a Kokoro voice name"},
    "response_format": {"type": "string", "description": "Ignored by Kokoro, which only makes WAV"},
    "speed": {"type": "number"}
  }
}
```

Response `200` (`audio/mpeg`) — the backend's audio bytes, labelled `audio/mpeg` by LiteLLM whatever they are (only a Gemini TTS model gets `audio/wav`): from kokoro they are WAV (`RIFF…WAVE`).

item.name: Chain aliases
item.description: The four LiteLLM chain aliases (ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml > CHAIN ALIASES), and `auto`, which the route-policy engine routes to one of them. Each chain is a model group with `order: 1 / 2 / 3` deployments; the overflow hook (ai/litellm/hooks/overflow) drops a busy or down local deployment so the next order answers. Call a chain directly with a key allowed it (the collection's {{virtual master key}}). LITELLM.md > Chain aliases and the overflow hook. Called directly, a chain alias gets NO backend footer: the `---` / `*<model> · <chain>*` footer is added only to responses for model `auto`. Here, read the deployment that answered from the `x-litellm-model-group` / `x-litellm-model-id` response headers or the spend log. LITELLM.md > The `auto` footer.

header.description: Optional: the chat id the route-policy service logs the decision under (GET /v1/route-policy/chats/postman-smoke-1/decisions). Open WebUI sends it with ENABLE_FORWARD_USER_INFO_HEADERS.

request.description:
Model `auto` -- routed by the route-policy engine (ai/route-policy) in ONE pass: the LiteLLM pre-call hook awaits the service's POST /decide (at most ROUTE_POLICY_DECIDE_TIMEOUT_S, 0.25 s) and rewrites the request to the chain alias it chose (local-general / local-code / local-reasoning / local-private); LiteLLM then serves that chain, streamed. `auto` is router_settings.model_group_alias -> local-private, so a request the engine did not route -- /decide slow, failing or apply=false, or the client off -- is served by local-private, the chain with no Claude.

Returns a normal chat completion (`model` stays `auto`). The answer ends with a footer naming what served it, e.g. `---` / `*qwen3.8-solo · local-code*`; `· route-policy fallback` means local-private served it because the engine did not route it, `· overflow (local busy)` that a Claude deployment answered. The `x-litellm-model-group` response header names the chain. The decision (every evaluator's vote) and its outcome are in the route-policy service: GET /v1/route-policy/chats/{chat id}/decisions with the X-OpenWebUI-Chat-Id sent here. POST /v1/messages with model `auto` is routed the same way. LITELLM.md > Route policy: single-pass `auto`; LITELLM.md > The `auto` footer.

#### Schemas

See *OpenAI-compatible / POST /v1/chat/completions*, the first request of this endpoint.

Chain alias `local-general` -- the route-policy engine's default route for `auto`. Orders: qwen3.8-solo (1) -> muse-glimmer (2) -> claude-sonnet-5 (3, overflow only). Each deployment calls its backend directly; a prompt over 114688 tokens skips qwen3.8-solo via the overflow hook's context fit.

Returns a normal chat completion. Check the spend log: model group local-general, model = the deployment that answered. A Claude row means the overflow hook dropped both local deployments (`make -s logs litellm FOLLOW=0 TAIL=all | grep overflow`) or both failed at call time. 401 = your key is not allowed local-general. LITELLM.md > Chain aliases and the overflow hook.

#### Schemas

See *OpenAI-compatible / POST /v1/chat/completions*, the first request of this endpoint.

Chain alias `local-code` -- where the route-policy engine sends `auto` when the chat is code (a code-like message, or a sandbox / Open Terminal tool called recently). A direct call to `local-general` is never moved here. Same ladder as local-general: qwen3.8-solo (1) -> muse-glimmer (2) -> claude-sonnet-5 (3, overflow only). What it adds, per deployment: a coding system prompt (litellm_system_prompt, merged in front of your first system message), deeper reasoning (qwen chat_template_kwargs reasoning_effort high, muse reasoning_strength xhigh) and max_tokens 32768 on the local orders.

The request's own `max_tokens` (512 here) overrides the deployment's 32768 -- drop it to get the coding default. A request `extra_body` or `chat_template_kwargs` REPLACES the deployment's (dropping the reasoning kwarg), it does not merge.

Spend log: model group local-code. 401 = key not allowed local-code. LITELLM.md > local-code: what it adds.

#### Schemas

See *OpenAI-compatible / POST /v1/chat/completions*, the first request of this endpoint.

Chain alias `local-reasoning` -- where the route-policy engine sends a reasoning request for `auto`. Orders: muse-glimmer (1) -> qwen3.8-solo (2) -> claude-opus-5-5 (3, overflow only). muse-glimmer's 8 sequences are shared with the classifier, which takes at most 6 (max_concurrent of the muse-glimmer entry in ai/classifier/models.yaml) and leaves 2 for chat; when chat needs more than those 2 the overflow hook may mark it busy and this lands on qwen3.8-solo.

Spend log: model group local-reasoning; an anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 row is Opus overflow. LITELLM.md > Chain aliases and the overflow hook.

#### Schemas

See *OpenAI-compatible / POST /v1/chat/completions*, the first request of this endpoint.

Chain alias `local-private` -- LOCAL ONLY. Orders: qwen3.8-solo (1) -> muse-glimmer (2), and NO Claude deployment, NO entry in `fallbacks` / `context_window_fallbacks`. The route-policy engine's privacy route lands here, and so does every `auto` request the engine did not route (/decide slow, failing or apply=false, or the client off) -- the `auto` alias itself points here. With both local models busy the overflow hook keeps them and the request queues in vLLM (slow, never cloud); with both down it fails (5xx) -- that is the guarantee working.

Spend log: model group local-private must ONLY ever show openai/qwen3.8-solo or openai/muse-glimmer. LITELLM.md > Chain aliases and the overflow hook.

#### Schemas

See *OpenAI-compatible / POST /v1/chat/completions*, the first request of this endpoint.

item.name: Admin
item.description: Management endpoints that require the LiteLLM master key. Each item overrides the collection-level Bearer to use `{{litellm master key}}` (value of `DEFAULT_LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` in `.env`, read by `general_settings.master_key`). Use these to issue and revoke virtual keys, inspect users, and enumerate model config from the DB. See LITELLM.md § `litellm_config.yaml` settings and the linked LiteLLM Config Settings reference for the DB-backed model-management flow.

query.description: User id to look up. Set the `userId` collection variable first.

item.name: Pass-through
item.description: Reverse proxies to internal services declared under `general_settings.pass_through_endpoints` in litellm_config.yaml. Every request keeps the caller's `Authorization` header (`forward_headers: true`) and `include_subpath: true` so anything after the mount prefix is passed through unchanged. This means downstream services see the LiteLLM virtual-key Bearer and can authenticate against it. Seven pass-throughs are mounted in this deployment: classifier, detector, madlad, interceptor, roofix, sandbox, route-policy. Every one has `auth: true`: LiteLLM rejects a missing or invalid key (401), and a non-admin virtual key also needs the route in its (or its team's) `metadata.allowed_passthrough_routes` or it gets 403 — the master key needs nothing extra. See ai/litellm/LITELLM.md § Pass-through auth.

item.name: MCP
item.description:
LiteLLM advertises MCP servers to clients (Claude Code, Open WebUI, custom apps) via the `mcp_servers` block in litellm_config.yaml. Each entry is mounted at `/mcp/{key}` — the key MUST match the URL path a client points at. LITELLM_MCP.md explains the tool-call loop; LiteLLM only surfaces the tool definitions to the model — YOU orchestrate the actual tool execution and feed the result back with the `tool` role message.

Mounted MCP servers in this deployment (from `mcp_servers`):
- `kokoro_tts` → http://kokoro-api:8000/mcp (TTS)
- `madlad_translate` → http://madlad-api:8000/mcp (translation)
- `detector` → http://detector:8000/mcp (open-vocabulary boxes — detect_objects)
- `interceptor` → http://interceptor:8080/mcp (CDP capture)
- `sandbox` → http://sandbox-runner:8000/mcp (get_runtime_types + create + write_files + read_file + edit_file + get_files + get_logs + exec + preview + close + list_sessions + run — see the sandbox-runner Postman collection's MCP folder for the FastMCP JSON-RPC calls)
- `trino` → http://trino-mcp:8080/mcp (federated read-only SQL — list_catalogs + list_schemas + list_tables + describe_table + run_query)
- `phoenix` → env-driven URL, bearer auth via `DEFAULT_LITELLM_MCP_PHOENIX_AUTH_VALUE`
- `gmail` → https://gmailmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1, OAuth2 (authorization_code, delegated to upstream)

Register these with Claude Code via `claude mcp add --transport http -s user {key} {litellm}/mcp/{key} --header "Authorization: Bearer sk-…"` — see LITELLM_MCP.md § Add MCP Servers to Claude Code.
